title: Schedule Times Added Durations Then Rolled Hours
text: id: COMP-008 domain: math title: Schedule Times Added Durations Then Rolled Hours tags: time, schedule, minutes memory: A schedule answer once came out an hour off because I added minutes in my head while crossing an hour boundary. I wrote the durations as one total minute count, converted to hours and leftover minutes, then added hours first and leftover minutes second. When the leftover minutes crossed 60, I carried one more hour instead of compressing the clock. The clock stopped being slippery once minutes had their own line.

title: Clock Carry Turned 160 Minutes Into 2 Hours 40 Minutes
text: id: COMP-022 domain: math title: Clock Carry Turned 160 Minutes Into 2 Hours 40 Minutes tags: schedule, time, clock, correction memory: I once added 160 minutes to a morning start time and landed almost two hours early. The correction was to convert first: 160 minutes is 2 hours 40 minutes. Starting at 9:15, adding 2 hours gives 11:15, then adding 40 minutes gives 11:55 AM. I remember writing the final line as: 160 minutes = 2 hours 40 minutes, so 9:15 AM + 2 hours 40 minutes = 11:55 AM. The carry across the hour was the whole problem.

title: The Ten Twenty Five Clock Error Cost Me
text: id: COMP-026 domain: math title: The Ten Twenty Five Clock Error Cost Me tags: schedule, time, negative-outcome, correction memory: I once wrote 10:25 AM after adding 160 minutes to 9:15 AM, and the person using the schedule missed the real finish window. I had added minutes as if the clock were a decimal. The correction was painful and simple: 160 minutes equals 2 hours 40 minutes, 9:15 AM plus 2 hours is 11:15 AM, and plus 40 minutes is 11:55 AM. Since that miss, the answer 10:25 AM makes me stop and redo the clock carry.
